stem: Which statement best describes the typical timing of the pubertal growth spurt in girls compared with boys?

options.text: Girls have their growth spurt late in puberty, usually after menarche
Girls have their growth spurt early in puberty, whereas boys have theirs in mid-to-late puberty
Both girls and boys reach their peak height velocity at the same age
Boys have their growth spurt early in puberty, whereas girls have theirs in mid-to-late puberty
Girls do not have a distinct pubertal growth spurt

explanation: Early pubertal growth spurt in girls. Girls usually reach peak height velocity earlier than boys, with boys peaking later in mid-to-late puberty.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because girls typically peak before menarche, not after it.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because girls usually reach peak height velocity earlier in puberty, while boys peak later in mid-to-late puberty.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the pubertal growth spurt occurs earlier in girls than in boys.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because boys generally peak later than girls, not earlier.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because girls do have a distinct pubertal growth spurt, and it occurs early in puberty.

source.hint: Recall which gender finishes their primary height gain shortly after their first period.
